correctness.rationale: For the smooth finite-delay equations, the characteristic factor has one simple zero at the critical dose and every other spectral root strictly negative. A center eigenfunction has infected and phage slopes J and sigma_i, verified by symbolic identities. The exact susceptible equation yields u-dot = -kappa u squared plus cubic terms; smooth retarded center-manifold and stable-foliation theory gives local attraction/repulsion, equilibrium branch, and t-inverse asymptotics. Positive/negative kappa both occur for the exact single-phage parameter examples. The zero-kappa case and global basins are explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: At the exact dose threshold, linear stability is inconclusive in a biologically motivated, arbitrary-strain, multiple-delay model. The explicit net-growth coefficient combines burst-size, decay, delay and coinfection contributions, determines the forward/backward positive-equilibrium direction, and yields precise one-over-time extinction of susceptible and infected populations. Both signs occur under physical positive parameters, so the boundary is a substantive regime distinction rather than a routine numerical increment.
